summary: 14-day Nightscout data show good coverage and TIR 86.0% with average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, but time below range 5.1% and CV 32.6% dominate safety. Overnight and 19:00 local lows cluster against a 90 mg/dL target, while 14:00-17:00 highs occur with zero carb announcements and UAM-led SMB. The selected AAPS profile is treated as applicable; meal strategy was declared empty and matches unlogged execution. One conservative review axis is overnight target only.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM is usable for pattern review. Coverage 98.7%, good quality, 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, no invalid or duplicate glucose rows. Profile segments and SMB settings are complete. Carb and e-carb streams are empty, so meal-linked inferences stay limited.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid entries of 4046 expected; 2315 treatments; 655 insulin entries totaling 275.95 U; 0 carb entries; 24 local hourly rows; authoritative aaps_profile with 7 basal, 5 CR, 1 ISF, 3 target segments, DIA 10 h.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No activity log and only representative treatments and loop snapshots, not the full device-status stream.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety brake is hypoglycemia and variability, not lack of time in range. Lows cluster overnight and around 19:00 local, with nadirs 41-42 mg/dL. Afternoon highs cluster 14:00-17:00. GLP-1 notes and an Aug 19 occlusion are episodic confounders. No later step should add overnight insulin or chase afternoon peaks with extra basal while this below-range pattern remains.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall TBR 5.1%, TAR 8.9%, TIR 86.0%, CV 32.6%. Local TBR h1 18.5% and h19 15.3%. Local TAR h16 32.1%. Extremes 41-42 and 286-293 mg/dL. Temporary targets of 135 mg/dL used repeatedly.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality supports glucose-clock conclusions; missing hypo-treatment notes do not remove the TBR signal.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No hypo-treatment or exercise log around the 41-42 mg/dL events.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight means sit near 90-106 mg/dL but the distribution is too low for a 90 mg/dL target. 04:00-08:00 is the most stable fasting-like window. Daytime rise from 09:00 and the 16:00 basal cut coincide with unannounced-meal hours, so they are not clean basal tests. The 18:00-19:00 crash sits on both rising evening basal and peak afternoon IOB, so 00:00 and 16:00-19:00 basal changes stay unsupported.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly means and TBR/TAR; basal 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.7/0.5/0.6/0.7 U/h; targets 90 then 100 then 90 mg/dL; frequent TT 135 contaminates daytime windows.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview forbids adding overnight insulin; meal and IOB effects are not separated.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting flags and cob always 0, so overnight IOB versus basal remains entangled.

analysis_steps.findings: CR cannot be tested. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is stronger than a simple TDD heuristic and is further strengthened by DynISF when glucose is high. DIA 10 h can carry afternoon UAM into overnight. Therapy-response windows are contaminated corrections, not ISF experiments. No CR, ISF, or DIA change is supported.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0 g carbs; cob 0 in representative loop rows; TDD about 19.7 U/day; loop variable_sens often about 28-71 when high and 80-124 when low; correction windows include -178 and -168 mg/dL after stacked insulin.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets overnight pattern may be IOB tail; safety_overview limits stronger effective insulin.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal composition and no clean ISF test after a stable basal period.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are the live meal controller. Activation is internally consistent for a no-announced-carb setup. Always-on SMB with a 3-minute interval can stack insulin on rises before guards cut. High temporary targets suppress SMB and help explain some afternoon peaks. Delivery-minute caps do not fully describe custom UAM boost sizes seen in reason text.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled and uam_enabled true; smb_always true; cob-related SMB flags false; interval 3 min; max SMB 15 min; max UAM SMB 20 min; high-TT SMB false; representative IOB 2.2-5.9 U on highs; cob 0.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR; unused CR; overnight lows compatible with SMB tail plus target 90.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Full SMB time series is not in the package; custom boost logic is only visible in reason strings.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off, so overnight lows are not Autosens target-lowering. DynISF at 70% makes effective ISF much stronger on afternoon peaks and can feed the evening crash. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U are wide rails; live basal cap in snapshots is about 4 U/h and hypos occur far below max IOB. Carb-absorption knobs are idle.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens false; dynISF true at 70%; variable_sens and sensitivity_ratio fields; temps capped near 4 U/h; min_5m_carbimpact 8; meal_max_absorption 7 h; 0 carb entries.
analysis_steps.dependencies: profile ISF 56 and DIA 10 h; SMB/UAM stage; safety TBR.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact DynISF formula and insulin-peak interaction are not fully specified.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so no representative prebolus or immediate-bolus percent exists. Observed execution matches that declaration: correction boluses and UAM/SMB only. Small corrections often precede large rises, which is unannounced intake rather than a finished meal bolus.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context.meal_strategies []; 0 carb entries; therapy windows all Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false; insulin 275.95 U; recurring TT 135.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused; SMB/UAM is the meal path; ISF, DynISF, DIA, and overnight target set hypo risk if more meal insulin is added.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Typical meal-start clock times are not declared or logged.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are unused. Absorption settings are not creating phantom COB. Unannounced rises lasting 60-180 minutes are not an e-carb recipe. Adding e-carbs would stack a second insulin trigger on always-on UAM.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries empty; extended_carb_entries 0; average_extended_carb_duration_min null; all response windows is_extended_carbs false.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked carb amount, start offset, or e-carb duration to review.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked accounts: unannounced intake plus UAM/DynISF delay explains 14:00-17:00 highs then 18:00-19:00 lows; overnight TBR with near-target means fits target 90 plus residual IOB better than a proven 00:00 basal error; 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h is not a supported hole; CR and e-carbs are idle. Package overrides earlier temptation to retune CR or afternoon basal. One profile axis is selected: review raising overnight targets only. Automation, ISF, DIA, basal, and meal channels stay unchanged until that review is observed.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly TBR/TAR; empty declared meal plan; cob 0; DynISF 70% with strong high-BG variable_sens; profile_context historical_applicability yes; decision_inventory complete.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All prior stages; do not combine target change with basal, ISF, DIA, SMB, or DynISF.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal-start timestamps would most improve separation of UAM delay from overnight IOB versus target.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7% with good quality and a complete selected profile.
Overall TIR 86.0% and average glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Local 04:00-08:00 is relatively stable with very little above-range time.
Closed loop remains active and does issue low temps when predicted guards are low.
Declared empty meal plan matches observed cob 0 and UAM-first execution, so there is no hidden CR conflict to reconcile first.
High temporary targets of 135 mg/dL are already used as a short shield.
issues: Overnight local TBR is high, especially 23:00-03:00, against a 90 mg/dL target and nadirs in the low 40s.
A second hypo cluster appears around 18:00-19:00 after afternoon highs.
Afternoon TAR peaks at 14:00-17:00 with no announced carbs, so UAM is late and then leaves residual IOB.
CV 32.6% and DynISF-amplified high-BG insulin couple the high-then-low shape.
An occlusion and pump error on Aug 19 plus GLP-1 notes add episodic noise.

recommendations.title: Review a higher overnight target only
recommendations.description: Overnight means already sit near 90-106 mg/dL while local TBR is 10-18% from 23:00-03:00. That is a setpoint-versus-risk mismatch, not a proven basal hole. Raising only the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 to 100 mg/dL aligns them with the existing 08:00 target and reduces overnight insulin pressure without adding afternoon insulin.

recommendations.title: Hold DynISF and SMB until the target review is observed
recommendations.description: DynISF 70% with always-on UAM remains the leading account of 14:00-17:00 TAR then 18:00-19:00 TBR, but it is dependent on ISF, DIA, and target. Changing those in the same step would prevent interpretation. Keep automation until several nights after any overnight-target review.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Review raising the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL and keep every other profile segment unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Local overnight TBR is high while average overnight glucose is already near or above 90 mg/dL. The 08:00 target is already 100 mg/dL, so 100 mg/dL is an existing user setpoint rather than a new invented number. Basal, CR, ISF, and DIA remain entangled with unannounced meals, UAM, DynISF, and DIA tail, so they stay unchanged.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After several nights with only this target review, compare local 23:00-03:00 TBR and mean glucose; if TBR stays high while overnight means sit clearly above 100 mg/dL, review evening residual IOB next rather than raising target again.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight means are near target but TBR is high, so residual IOB and the 90 mg/dL target remain competing explanations. Evidence does not isolate 00:00 basal as high. Uncertainty is medium. Depends on target review and evening UAM tail before any basal edit.
Local 04:00-07:00 is the most stable window with low TAR and modest TBR. No fasting defect is isolated. Depends on leaving dawn basal untouched while overnight target is the only review axis.
Aggregate 06:00-08:00 means stay near 100-110 mg/dL with little above-range time. The isolated Aug 21 42 mg/dL near 07:19 is not the hourly pattern. Change unsupported.
Late-morning rise overlaps unannounced intake and UAM, not a fasting basal test. Raising 10:00 basal would add insulin into a high-TBR day. Depends on unresolved meals.
Hour 16 has the highest TAR, but UAM is already the afternoon actuator and the following 18:00-19:00 crash argues against adding basal here. Meal and IOB effects are not separated.
Local 18:00-19:00 includes the steepest fall and 41-42 mg/dL extremes after afternoon IOB. A basal increase is unsafe; a decrease is not separable from UAM tail. Keep pending target observation.
Hour 19 TBR 15.3% sits on this segment and on residual afternoon insulin. Evidence does not isolate 0.7 U/h as the cause. Depends on DIA, SMB, and DynISF remaining unchanged in the same step.
Zero carb entries and cob 0 mean this CR is unused. No meal-linked evidence supports a change. Uncertainty is high if logging starts later.
No carb treatments occur in this segment. Changing an unused CR would not explain current telemetry.
Afternoon and late-morning TAR occur without announced carbs, so this is a UAM pattern, not a measured weak 08:00 CR.
Stronger evening CR could theoretically add to 18:00-19:00 drops only if meal boluses were given. Telemetry shows no carb boluses. Change unsupported.
Unused with cob 0. Overnight TBR is better explained by target and residual IOB than by this CR.

ISF 56 is stronger than a TDD heuristic and DynISF makes it stronger still when high, but correction windows are stacked with SMB and site events. Changing ISF together with target or DynISF is forbidden. Evidence, uncertainty, and automation dependence all favor keep.

Local 00:00-03:00 TBR is 10-18% while means are already about 90-106 mg/dL. A review candidate of 100 mg/dL matches the existing 08:00 target and loosens overnight insulin without claiming basal is proven high. Uncertainty remains because DIA-tail IOB can contribute. Depends on not changing basal, ISF, or SMB in the same step.
Daytime 100 mg/dL is already the less aggressive setpoint. Afternoon TAR is meal/UAM, not a low daytime target. Keep as the alignment value for overnight review.
This segment starts the overnight 90 mg/dL window where TBR rises from 23:00. Same review direction as 00:00, one overnight axis only. Depends on observing several nights before any automation edit.
A 10 h DIA can explain overnight tail from afternoon UAM, but there is no clean insulin-action study. Changing DIA with target would confound the only selected review. Keep.

This pair is the actual meal path with cob 0. Turning it off would leave unannounced rises without a declared bolus plan. No source component is null, so verify is not used. Hold until after target observation.
Flags are consistent for UAM-first therapy. High-TT SMB off already provides a shield. Changing always-on in the same step as overnight target would hide the cause of any TBR change.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Interval and UAM minutes can stack insulin, but custom boost text means these caps do not fully describe delivered SMB. Change unsupported until meal-start times and a single-axis target review exist. No null components, so keep not verify.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Hypos occur well below 25 U IOB and live temps hit about 4 U/h, not 12 U/h. Limits are unused headroom, not the demonstrated cause. Tightening them is not the first safe review.

DynISF 70% likely amplifies afternoon dosing, but it depends on ISF 56 and SMB. Autosens is already off. A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not disabled Autosens. Hold this group so the overnight target review stays interpretable.
No carb or e-carb entries, so these knobs are idle and are not phantom COB. UAM is a separate path. Change unsupported.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the declared and observed plan: no prebolus, no immediate bolus percentage, no e-carbs, and meal insulin from UAM plus always-on SMB only, with optional small corrections and occasional 135 mg/dL temporary targets as a high-target shield.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: analysis_context.meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so there is no declared prebolus or bolus split to reproduce. Telemetry matches that declaration with 0 g carbs, cob 0, and correction or SMB insulin only. Adding e-carbs or a bolus percent would stack another insulin channel on DynISF, ISF 56, DIA 10 h, and overnight target 90 while TBR is already the safety brake.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record clock times when typical eating starts, even without grams, for several days.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring local 14:00-19:00 unannounced rise then fall
exceptions.suggestion: Do not add e-carbs or a CR-based bolus percent for this cluster while carbs remain unlogged.
exceptions.rationale: This is the same UAM-only strategy with a worse IOB tail, not a second documented meal recipe.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring temporary target 135 mg/dL for about 30-180 minutes, often late morning to afternoon
exceptions.suggestion: Treat this as a high-target SMB mute, not as a prebolus or e-carb substitute.
exceptions.rationale: smb_with_high_temp_target is false, so larger peaks in those hours are expected and are not a missing immediate-bolus percent.

implementation_steps: Confirm the selected aaps_profile is the profile actually running, including the overnight 90 mg/dL targets and DynISF 70%.
If a change is reviewed, discuss only the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 to 100 mg/dL. Leave basal, CR, ISF, DIA, SMB, UAM, DynISF, limits, and absorption untouched in that same step.
Independently verify any change, apply at most one axis, and monitor overnight and evening glucose closely for several days.
After that observation window, compare local 23:00-03:00 TBR and mean glucose with the 14:00-19:00 high-then-low shape before considering a later DynISF or SMB-frequency review.
Collect typical meal-start clock times so a future meal-channel discussion can be evidence-based rather than adding e-carbs onto UAM.
education: Time-in-range can look acceptable while overnight time-below-range is still the binding risk. Averages hide that distribution.
With cob 0, carb ratio and e-carb settings are not steering the loop. Unannounced-meal SMB is a separate path and is not extra carb counting.
Dynamic ISF can make a listed ISF much stronger at high glucose, so high-then-low swings may be automation plus residual IOB rather than a simple basal hole.
E-carbs are not a pump extended bolus. They should not be inferred from an unused average duration field.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely. TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
Nadirs of 41-42 mg/dL, overall TBR 5.1%, and local 19:00 plus overnight hypo clusters limit any added insulin, including afternoon basal, stronger ISF, or new e-carbs.
Do not change dependent settings together. Overnight target review and DynISF or SMB edits in the same step would make the result uninterpretable.
Discuss profile ideas with the care team before changing AAPS. Do not change AAPS automatically.
